sections.title: Overview
sections.body: The previous corrective RAG example had a retrieval and rewriting loop. A production agentic workflow requires additional authorization, budgets, fallback routing, state persistence and verification.

steps.label: Query
steps.narration: The user query enters the system and may need rewriting before search.

steps.label: Transform
steps.narration: Query transformation expands, rewrites, or decomposes the question to improve recall.

steps.label: Search
steps.narration: Dense and/or keyword search return candidate passages.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.narration: Fusion methods such as RRF combine rankings from multiple retrievers into one list.

steps.label: Rerank
steps.narration: A cross-encoder or LLM reranker reorders candidates for higher precision context.

steps.label: Context
steps.narration: Final context is budgeted, ordered, and injected into the prompt for grounded generation.

sections.title: 33.1 Production state design
sections.body:
```python
from typing import TypedDict, Literal

class ProductionRAGState(TypedDict):

    request_id: str

    question: str
    search_query: str

    route: Literal[
        "hybrid",
        "sql",
        "multimodal"
    ]

    candidate_ids: list[str]
    selected_evidence_ids: list[str]

    missing_requirements: list[str]

    attempts: int
    max_attempts: int

    remaining_token_budget: int

    context_sufficient: bool
    context_authorized: bool

    answer: str
    answer_verified: bool

    outcome: Literal[
        "pending",
        "success",
        "abstain",
        "blocked",
        "error"
    ]
```

Security identities and authorization policy should be supplied through trusted runtime context or independently resolved services. The LLM must not be allowed to modify the authenticated principal or expand its permissions through graph state.

sections.title: 33.2 Deterministic control routing
33.3 LangGraph production controls
sections.body:
| Capability | Production consideration |
|--------|--------|
| Conditional edges | Enforce deterministic security and budget rules |
| Checkpointing | Protect persisted conversation and document data |
| Human-in-the-loop | Review high-risk operations and uncertain content |
| Parallel nodes | Prevent uncontrolled fan-out |
| Agent memory | Prevent cross-user or persistent poisoning |
| Tool execution | Validate authorization and arguments |
| State restoration | Revalidate current access permissions |
| Retry policies | Avoid retry amplification |
| Recursion limits | Prevent infinite agent cycles |
| Streaming | Ensure unauthorized text is not emitted before checks |

A checkpoint is not merely technical state. It can contain confidential business information and must be protected accordingly.

steps.narration: A client request arrives at the gateway with identity and policy context.

steps.label: Auth
steps.narration: Virtual keys authenticate the caller; authorization checks tenant and scope.

steps.label: Policy
steps.narration: Rate limits, quotas, and safety policies are enforced before spend happens.

steps.label: Route
steps.narration: Routing chooses provider/model based on quality, cost, latency, or fallback rules.

steps.narration: The upstream model generates tokens under timeout and retry controls.
